text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-2789 — hosted/generate p95 latency > 1200ms (5m window). Link: https://pagerduty/redwood/PD-2789

pagerduty: paging @maya (oncall) — escalation policy: eng-oncall-primary

maya: acked. looking at grafana now. can someone post traces if they see errors? :eyes:

jon.h: seeing a big tail in latency around 03:01 UTC, but errors are flat. mostly 200s just slow.

lee: checking autoscaler logs — scaled a replica at 03:02 but late. also seeing a burst of many tiny requests from internal service load-checker-2 targeting /v1/generate with tiny contexts.

sam: hmm we ran a cache compaction/evict job earlier (scheduled) at 03:00. could be a KV cache churn causing cold-kv misses and slower decodes. Toni, did you run anything manual?

toni: I kicked off the compaction job at 02:59 as part of the memory-maintenance run. expected some temporary miss-rate increase but not >1s p95.

incident-bot: Alert auto-resolved at 03:06 UTC — PD-2789 resolved (metric back under threshold).

maya: silenced PD (auto-resolved) and acked the thread. short lived, but noisy. anyone see customer-facing errors?

jon.h: no 4xx/5xx spike in customer metrics. only internal synthetic probes showed the hit. looks like no-customer-impact. :relieved:

lee: logged two things: (1) cache compaction + coincident internal synthetic load created transient latency tail, (2) overlap between two PD rules caused duplicate triggers. filed INFR-612 to dedupe composite+base rules.

sam: adding a quick note — autoscaler cold-starts are ~30-45s; with cache churn that was additive. Recommend we add a short hatch window where we suppress alerting until autoscale completes for this route.

maya: agreed. i'll create a follow-up task for alert gating + add schedule constraint for maintenance windows. also marking post-incident tag: "transient-noise-autoresolve".

toni: FYI the maintenance run had a flag to avoid wide invalidations but one config drifted on the compaction script. i'll revert the flag and run in canary tomorrow.

jon.h: can we also add a small metric rule to surface repeated auto-resolves (flapping) so we can catch noisy thresholds?

lee: good idea. will add to runbook: if PD auto-resolves within 10m and incidents>3 in 1h, open carry-forward ticket.

maya: cool. no immediate customer impact, moving to post-mortem-lite. I'll summarize timeline and actions in #postmortems tomorrow. thanks all. :thumbsup:

pagerduty: note: PD incident PD-2789 has no escalations outstanding; all pagers cleared.

sam: leaving a small snippet of the trace that correlated with spike:

```
span: decode_kv_cache_miss 03:01:22.453 - duration=420ms
span: model_infer_queue_wait 03:01:22.876 - duration=180ms
```

maya: attaching to the follow-up ticket: INFR-612 (dedupe rules), INFR-613 (alert gating), MAINT-89 (compaction config fix).

lee: flagged for next oncall rotation to keep an eye on similar compaction windows.

maya: closing thread here — will post RCA summary tomorrow. if anything else pops up, re-open. :white_check_mark:
